title: Normalized chains include by a chain homotopy equivalence
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and $X$ a simplicial object of $\mathcal A$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Let $N(X)$ be the nonnegative chain complex with $N(X)_0=X_0$ and $N(X)_n=\bigcap_{i=1}^n\ker(d_i:X_n\to X_{n-1})$ for $n>0$, with differential $d_0$ in positive degrees and zero out of degree zero. Let $C(X)_n=X_n$ with differential $\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^id_i$ for $n\ge1$ and zero out of degree zero. The canonical inclusion $N(X)\to C(X)$ is a chain homotopy equivalence: it has a chain-map inverse up to chain homotopy. Here a homotopy from $f$ to $g$ is a family $h_n$ of degree-one maps satisfying $f-g=dh+hd$. The inclusions form a natural transformation in $X$.

source.place: Choudhury–Gallauer, Homotopy theory of dg sheaves, Fact 3.14(1), printed p. 11; normalization with kernels of d_1,...,d_n and differential d_0, as in Mathlib MooreComplex.lean:64-90, rather than the equivalent opposite-face normalization of the paper.
